decision: Build v1.3 around one typed change review instead of adding repository-wide signals
why: The current product already has validated signals but leaves the final change decision to prompt prose

decision: Use high rigor and land through a feature branch
why: The change crosses the domain model, CLI, MCP, plugin hook, cache behavior, and public documentation

decision: Keep dashboards, PR-process metrics, telemetry, and wider language parsing out of scope
why: Those ideas were deliberately cut and do not tighten the current change-review loop

decision: Select candidate 1 as the base and graft candidate 2's pure ranker plus candidate 3's explicit no-change result
why: It is the smallest design that preserves precise base, staged, and working-tree semantics with one uncached policy boundary
evidence: three architecture candidates and gpt-5.6-terra cross-judge scorecard

decision: Keep the ambient hook narrow and parse its JSON in Python
why: A full fresh review after every edit would be slow and noisy; the explicit command owns the complete decision
result: jq dependency removed without moving full review into the hook

decision: Defer complexity-growth actions until a threshold is validated
why: An arbitrary delta threshold would create a new unvalidated recommendation policy; v1.3 can expose current complexity while grounding actions in measured history

decision: Capture the release acceptance failure before implementation
why: The current ratio-first sorter puts a 1-of-1 pair ahead of repeated 11-of-13 evidence and no change-review entry point exists
evidence: focused pytest: 5 failed, 12 passed, 2 collection errors

decision: Use a 95% Wilson lower bound and a two-shared-revision action floor
why: The ordering remains statistically named and auditable while preventing one-off perfect ratios from dominating

decision: Keep review uncached and keep the ambient hook on its small HEAD-aware cache
why: Dirty working-tree review cannot be made truthful with the existing process cache, while a full scan after every edit would be noisy
evidence: MCP freshness test, guard HEAD invalidation test, direct CLI run
result: Review is fresh and the hook stays fast

decision: Add the companion tests named by the real review output
why: The new command ranked analysis.py to test_analysis.py first with 11 shared revisions, exposing a real test coverage gap
result: Regression assertions now cover raw counts and ensured paths

decision: Share coupling display projection and bound primary review evidence
why: The thermo-nuclear and deslop pass found duplicated projection code and an unbounded coupling list

decision: Verify the actual package, command, adapters, and test suite
why: The release must pass through real artifacts rather than mocks alone
evidence: 339 tests, 95% coverage, ruff, build, direct doctor, direct review, scripts/verify_change_review.py

decision: Clarify the support floor is the default
why: The CLI and MCP intentionally expose min_shared_revisions so an explicit caller can lower it to one
result: Documentation now matches the public option

why: Additional type-boundary regression coverage was added after the first green row
evidence: 340 tests passed in the final reviewer run
result: The latest verification count is authoritative

why: The gpt-5.6-terra trail review proved working-tree review resolved HEAD before collecting an untracked first file
evidence: real unborn working-tree and staged integration coverage
result: HEAD is nullable for local modes and untracked first files review successfully

decision: Align clean-result and guard documentation contracts
why: The plugin must report CI state even when no paths are selected, and the guard docstring still named ratio-first ordering
result: NoChanges carries disabled CI status and docs name Wilson ordering

why: The unborn-repository regression test was added after the earlier correction
evidence: 341 tests at 95.54% coverage, ruff, release proof, diff check

decision: Accept the cross-model re-review after fixes
